This row read 4.5 % on basis field_range - the geometric middle of two Punjab coalfields' RESOURCE ranges, which the register preamble itself defines as 'a RANGE of what the seams hold, not the average burned'. It is now 4.643 % on basis measured_avg, the mean of the three as-fired analyses held, and is the FIRST ROW IN THIS REGISTER EVER TO USE measured_avg: the vocabulary has declared that word since rc58 and no row had earned it. The level barely moves (+3.2 %, national brick SO2 225.3 -> 232.4 kt); the DERIVATION moves from what is in the ground to what was burned. THE OLD DERIVATION WAS WRONG INDEPENDENTLY OF ITS VALUE. Both measured Punjab kilns fire BALOCHISTAN and HYDERABAD (Sindh) coal, bought at Rs. 14,000 and Rs. 9,000 per tonne; price selects sulfur before geology does, and a central built from Salt Range and Makarwal resource ranges was describing seams these kilns do not buy from. THE BAND IS THE OBSERVED RANGE AND IS ASYMMETRIC ABOUT THE CENTRAL (-2.26 / +1.31), which the loader permits and which is what three real batches look like. hi drops 10.7 -> 5.95 because a resource maximum has no place in a measured row; lo stays 2.38, the lowest analysis held. UNCERT_PCT DELIBERATELY STAYS AT 60 AND WAS NOT NARROWED TO MATCH THE NEW BASIS. Three samples spanning a factor of 2.5 do not license a precision claim: the standard error of the mean is 24.6 % and a t-interval on n=3 is about +/- 106 %, so 60 sits inside what the sample supports. It is also floored by the retention term - 0.25 +/- 100 % contributes 33.3 in quadrature - and retention is explicitly NOT closed (gap brick-sulfur-retention), so buying precision in the sulfur term would be spent immediately. Relabelling a row measured_avg already makes it look tighter than three batches justify; narrowing the uncertainty at the same time would compound that. Every source says its figure is a batch and not an average. WHAT IS STILL MISSING is a sampling design, not another anecdote. The repair is correct and it is not a lever.
